cells.tense: Right now, something a group of you share is being passed along and reshaped as it goes.
cells.act: blend the two things instead of choosing one
cells.ask: Where two versions of the same practice both still work, use them side by side this week rather than choosing, and carry the pair through one ordinary evening without collapsing it.
cells.core:
You can hand down what a group of you share and keep it soft at the edges — close to the living people you're actually with, still shaped by wherever it came from. When the crowd shifts, when a different age or a different question turns up, what you carry bends to meet it and doesn't break. Nothing gets defended; it just keeps working.

Two versions get offered and you set them side by side rather than choosing. Small corrections as things move, not a lurch. The cost is that nothing settles for good — you tend it again next time. A shared thing that moves with its people stays recognisable a year on, and that is what you'll have.
cells.sheetLine: You pass it on and it keeps changing shape.
cells.place: clean ground before anything is planted

cells.tense: Later on, what a group of you share will be held so tightly that no new person can get a grip on it.
cells.act: stand in the gap it leaves without rebuilding yet
cells.ask: Pick a rule you've defended as if it were the whole of it, stop propping it, and stay where it was with nothing there rather than filling it.
cells.core:
Later on, the shared thing you carry will be gripped so hard the people meant to receive it can't reach it, and you'll be braced against your own crowd. Something is locked down before it's been felt — the letters crowding out what the letters were for. That grip feels like care and lands as pressure on whoever you want to belong.

Loosen one hand. Pick a rule you've kept standing as if it were the whole tradition and set it down. Then leave the space where it stood for a while instead of filling it. What comes away was already cracked; what stays is the practice's real body, lighter, and people can come close again.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the text so tight nothing can enter.
cells.place: clean ground before anything is planted

cells.tense: For a while now, what groups of people share has been out of reach, and each person has been rebuilding it alone.
cells.act: see how it works underneath, apart from this instance
cells.ask: Take one plain exchange you watched this week and look beneath it to how that kind of moment works, apart from the particular people in it.
cells.core:
Something shared sits inside you, and you've been outside it, building your own language one person at a time. That reach isn't gone; it's turned inward. What you carry hasn't found anyone to carry it with, so the same work gets done from scratch.

There's a way back that doesn't ask you to lean harder. Look at one plain exchange — how a handful of people answered the same moment this month — and notice how that kind of moment works underneath, apart from any single one of them. Try saying that mechanism in a single line. The shared thing you've been standing outside of is waiting to be joined.
cells.sheetLine: You know the shape. It hasn't found its people yet.
cells.place: clean ground before anything is planted

cells.tense: Right now, something shared moves through you to other people while you call yourself a learner.
cells.act: find the centre and hold it while things move
cells.ask: When someone asks you a real question, hold your centre while things move around you, answer from what you actually know, and stop there.
cells.core:
You are the one others gather around when something needs explaining, and if someone described your week back, you'd call yourself a student of it. The teaching is already happening — the person who feels like a learner is also the one handing things over. You keep it steady without believing you do.

Let something you've quietly carried for other people be seen as yours, in the words that come, and count your own hand in it. No pedestal needed. Standing in the middle of what's moving is what you already do; it just needs to be counted as yours, on purpose, before someone else has to point it out.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one others copy. You just don't count it.
cells.place: clean ground before anything is planted
